children: The benchmark indices corrected half a percent on September 7, with market breadth returning to negative. About 1,960 shares were under pressure, compared with 1,300 advancing shares on the NSE. The choppy trade with a weak bias may be seen in the near term. Here are some short-term trading ideas to consider:
Jigar S Patel, Senior Manager - Equity Research at Anand Rathi

Titagarh Rail Systems has bounced back from its recent lows and is now trading above its important moving averages — these act as dynamic support levels, and holding above them signals buyers are in control. The stock also broke above a descending trendline (a line connecting lower highs during a downtrend), which technically suggests the prior downward pressure may be easing and momentum could be turning upward.

The RSI (Relative Strength Index) at around 60 shows moderate bullish strength — it's above the neutral 50 mark but still has room before hitting overbought territory (above 70), so there's potential runway left. Traders may consider entering long positions in the Rs 890-870 zone.

AIA Engineering is trading near a confluence of technical supports, which makes this zone worth watching. It's close to the 50 percent retracement of its prior up move — a Fibonacci level where stocks often find support after giving back half a rally. This lines up with the 200-day exponential moving average (200-DEMA), a key long-term trend gauge, and also matches the previous breakout zone, where old resistance can turn into support once broken.

When several signals converge like this, it strengthens the case for a genuine demand zone where buyers may step in, offering a defined risk-reward setup. The idea would be to look for entries near this support cluster, with a stop-loss just below to cap downside if it fails, while a decisive move above the recent swing high would confirm renewed bullish momentum. Traders may consider entering long positions in the zone 4,250–4,200.

After a sharp, prolonged decline, HBL Engineering appears to have formed an "extended bottom" — three successive lows near the same support zone, suggesting selling pressure may be running out. Alongside this, the daily RSI shows bullish divergence: while price made equal or lower lows, RSI made higher lows, indicating weakening downside momentum since momentum is no longer confirming the price action.
The accompanying volume surge points to renewed buying interest or accumulation at these levels, adding weight to the pattern. Traders may consider entering long positions in the Rs 705- 695 zone.
Jay Thakkar, Vice President & Head of Derivatives and Quant Research at ICICI Securities
Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Futures | CMP: Rs 8,843

Apollo Hospitals has been consolidating in a range which is getting narrower now, however, overall there has been a clear up trend in the stock with increase in open interest indicating that the larger trend is positive. As per the options data, there has been Put additions at the lower levels indicating support and above that there has been Call unwinding as well right from Rs 8,600-9,000 strike indicating that the bulls have an upper hand until this range is not broken in the lower side.

The maximum pain is at Rs 8,800 strike and the stock has just managed to close above the same, hence any further up move from hereon will lead to a breakout on the upside. Buy Apollo Hospitals Futures in the range of Rs 8,800-8,850.

Divis Labs has shown a strong performance in the last few weeks and there has been overall long additions in this stock well supported by the options data too as when it broke above Rs 7,000 levels which had the highest Call base thereafter the overall trend has been in the grip of the bulls. So, far any profit booking has been bought into since the breakout and this time too the stock has been consolidating within a band of Rs 9,100-9,350 and a break above Rs 9,350 will lead to continuation of the on-going uptrend. Buy Divis Labs Futures in the range of Rs 9,330-9,350.

Blue Star has recently witnessed significant short additions and with that it has become oversold which is reflected in the price which is now not falling indicating a possibility of a bounce back due to short covering.

As per the options data, the Rs 1,500 strike has the highest Call base and above that it will lead to call unwinding. The maximum pain is also at Rs 1,500 and above that it will act as a support. Above Rs 1,500 strike there is no major Call base as well. Buy Blue Star Futures in the range of Rs 1,480-1,500.

title: Trade Spotlight: How should you trade Titagarh Rail Systems, AIA Engineering, Apollo Hospitals, Divis Labs, Blue Star, and others on September 8?
